messages.content: Can you predict the price of a house with an area of 2500 square feet, 3 rooms, constructed in the year 2000, and located in New York, and then compare it with the price of a similar house but with an area of 3000 square feet, constructed in the year 2005, and located in Los Angeles? Finally, predict the price of a third house with an area of 2000 square feet, 2 rooms, constructed in the year 1995, and located in Chicago.

function.name: predict_house_price
function.description: Predict house price based on area, number of rooms and year of construction. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

area.description: Area of the house in square feet.

rooms.description: Number of rooms in the house.

year.description: Year when the house was constructed.

location.description: The location or city of the house.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the tool `predict_house_price` twice (for first two houses) and once more for third house.

But we have three predictions:

1st house: area=2500, rooms=3, year=2000, location="New York"

2nd house: area=3000, rooms=?, they didn't specify rooms; maybe same as previous? They said "similar house" but only gave area/year/location. We can assume same number of rooms? But not specified. Might treat missing param as default? Probably we should ask clarifying question about rooms count. However user asked directly. Could interpret "similar house" meaning same features except area/year/location difference. So likely also 3 rooms. We'll use rooms=3.

Third house: area=2000, rooms=2, year=1995, location="Chicago".

We'll produce predictions via calling the function thrice.

Then provide comparison between first two predicted prices.

Let's do calls.
